Learning-to-defer generalizes rejection learning for combining automated and human decisions, which could inform a confidence-gated repair strategy (RQ5), but the paper's domain is classifier fairness, not PDF repair, so applicability here is speculative.
Presents a general constraint-guided data-repair framework directly relevant to structural repair strategies for damaged object graphs (RQ2, RQ5).
Describes exact and heuristic recovery of DEFLATE-compressed data at arbitrary offsets, directly applicable to repairing PDFs with corrupted FlateDecode streams (damage class C9, RQ1/RQ2).

Title indicates a file-carving method for deleted compressed files, methodologically adjacent to PDF stream/object carving (RQ2), but it targets NTFS compression sets rather than PDF structures, so transfer is uncertain and no abstract was retrievable to confirm.
Documents the specific Adler-32 weakness for small packets and its replacement with a CRC checksum, directly grounding the charter's checksum-verification and Adler-32-weakness discussion.

Proposes a syntactic method to reconstruct highly fragmented OOXML (ZIP-based) files by structural signature matching, directly analogous to the PDF object/xref carving needed for RQ2 even though the container format differs.

A deep-learning repair approach for damaged audio files could inform ML-based repair strategy (in-scope per charter), but the target modality is audio, not PDF, so relevance rests on method transfer alone and no abstract was retrievable.

Title and venue (black-box file repair, Digital Investigation) directly match the charter's repair-engine goal and RQ5 strategy focus; no abstract was retrievable so this is judged on bibliographic signal alone.
Title and JCDL venue indicate a benchmark for PDF text-extraction tools, directly useful for evaluation baselines relevant to RQ3 (text/fonts); the abstract was blocked by an IEEE bot-check.
Describes a vision-transformer OCR approach for turning PDF page images into structured markup, directly relevant to the charter's in-scope ML/VLM methods for text/font recovery (RQ3, RQ6).

Title ('Corrupted PDF recovery algorithm for digital forensic investigations') is unambiguously central to the charter's repair-engine goal; the abstract was unreachable behind a ScienceDirect redirect.

CNN-based font recognition/clustering for Hangul could support font-substitution or font-recovery techniques (RQ3), but is scoped to a single non-Latin script and a recognition (not repair) task, so relevance is partial; the abstract was blocked by a Springer challenge page.
Directly addresses text recovery from corrupted PDF documents (RQ3), matching the charter's core goal; the full paper was retrieved from the open-access ACL Anthology PDF.
A comprehensive, multi-source benchmark for document parsing (layout, OCR, tables) directly usable as an evaluation baseline for repaired-document fidelity (RQ3, Success criteria).
Benchmarks ten PDF metadata/reference/table extraction tools on a large arXiv-derived dataset, directly useful as an evaluation framework for the project's own extraction pipeline (RQ3/RQ5).

Proposes systematic extraction-and-reconstruction techniques for forensic messaging analysis that may transfer to PDF object/content reconstruction (RQ6), but the target domain (A2P/SMS messages) is unrelated to PDF, so relevance is indirect.

Title is a direct, unambiguous match to the charter's PDF-carving and memory-forensics scope (RQ2); no doi/arxiv/url exists so this is judged on title/venue alone.

The normative PDF 2.0 specification is the baseline reference for what constitutes a well-formed document, underlying the charter's damage-class and provenance-grade definitions; no URL is available but the identity is unambiguous.

Title and venue (Digital Investigation) propose a standardized classification scheme for recovered/repaired files, directly matching the charter's provenance-grade and forensic-fidelity definitions, though the abstract could not be retrieved.
A commercial online PDF-tools marketing page with no URL, no abstract, and no research content to assess against the charter's inclusion criteria.
An actively maintained index of PDF-centric test corpora, directly useful for sourcing the damaged and valid PDF datasets the charter's evaluation requires; the README was read in full.

A pragmatic PDF parsing/validation/normalization tool with a large-scale empirical study on 10k real-world files, directly on-topic for RQ2 (structure) and RQ4 (trust); full text confirms this is core, closely-scoped work.

Builds a large, web-crawled corpus of visually rich PDF documents, a candidate training/evaluation dataset for the charter's in-scope ML/VLM repair methods, despite the abstract being blocked behind a Springer challenge page.

Directly examines hidden-data exploitation and sanitization in real-world PDF files, matching the charter's in-scope CDR/sanitization methods, despite the abstract being unreachable behind an ACM access wall.
